commits.subject: Retract the superseded free-half claim WHERE IT LIVES, in FiberBound's own docstring
commits.summary:
**Correcting my own r4 text in place.** `FiberBound.lean` still said `baseChange_binders_stable` "is the whole of the free half" of extension-uniformity. It is not: class stability says nothing until an OBJECT carries the base-changed instances in the consumer`s spelling, and that lemma never mentions $C_\kappa$, so it witnesses no re-firing. Marked SUPERSEDED in the section docstring and on the declaration, pointing at `ExtensionUniformity.vanishing_baseChangeField`.

**Also flags the open-half mis-pricing at its source:** the paragraph blaming a non-transportable $n_0(\kappa)$ is wrong in the same file`s own terms, since the threshold is existential and monotone in $b$. A reader who stops at `FiberBound` would otherwise inherit both errors.

**Docstring-only:** every declaration line is byte-identical to HEAD (verified by diffing all signature/`variable`/`import`/`namespace` lines); the only apparent difference was a prose line beginning with the word "theorem" inside the replaced docstring. Kernel build 8691 exit 0, both modules rebuilt.

commits.subject: Locate the real deliverable for genus invariance: AJC owns both sides of the comparison, not the comparison
commits.summary:
**Measured, not assumed.** With the carriers `rfl`-equal there is an AJC-native route besides porting AJCR wholesale, and every brick of it is present at HEAD: `Adelic.LaurentChartData.pullbackSquare` builds a 2-affine cover on `C` from any finite $\pi$ (supplied by `MapToP1`), `Scheme.AffineCoverMVSquare.baseChangeField` transports it to $C_\kappa$, and `h1_unit_baseChangeField_eq_genus` already reads $h^1(\mathcal O_{C_\kappa})$ on that transported cover AS $\mathrm{genus}\,C_\kappa$.

**So the residue is one specific equivalence,** not a chapter: the termwise base-change comparison $\Gamma(C,V) \otimes_k \kappa \simeq \Gamma(C_\kappa, V_\kappa)$ on chart sections -- AJCR `relSectionsBaseChange`. AJC has both SIDES expressed on transported covers and lacks the map that makes them agree. That is the deliverable on either route.

**A second carrier boundary the rfl does NOT cover:** AJCR states its genus invariance over `AffineTwoCover`, AJC over `AffineCoverMVSquare`, and `AffineTwoCover` occurs nowhere in AJC. Object-level defeq of the base-changed curve says nothing about the cover carriers, so a port crosses two boundaries, not one.

commits.subject: The AJC/AJCR base-change carriers agree by rfl -- verified at my own spelling, with a negative control
commits.summary:
**Settled, and favourably.** An AJCR lane answered my thread question: `baseChangeBundle C K` and AJC `Over.mk (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k K))))` agree by `rfl` -- the whole BUNDLED object, structure morphism included. AJCR `⊗` is the monoidal product in `Over (Spec k)`, whose `tensorObj` is the pullback and `snd` is `pullback.snd`; the gap was notational.

**Re-verified rather than taken on report,** at `Scheme.baseChangeField` (the spelling my consumers bind), with a negative control: the same `rfl` with pullback arguments swapped fails on a type mismatch, so the check is not proving whatever it is handed.

**Status of input (1) moves from blocked to reachable-cost-unmeasured.** Two caveats kept: the verdict is defeq AT THE OBJECT and must be re-run through any functor a port applies; and carrier defeq is necessary but not sufficient, since the genus statements also bind AJCR `Curve.BaseChangeInstances` and its `curveCover`. It stays a hypothesis in the reduction -- an unmeasured port is not an available theorem.

commits.subject: Repair: my previous commit reverted three AJCR files it never touched
commits.summary:
**What happened.** `d2213eb83` was staged with `add <my two paths>` on an index I had re-seeded EARLIER in the session; between the re-seed and the commit, another lane landed work, so my tree was built from a stale base and silently reverted three AJCR paths -- unrooting `Tangent.DualNumberUnitTransport` from their root roll-up, reverting one Picard proof file, and deleting a 112KB `informal/spec-dd-r.md` that was still on disk.

**Repair is non-destructive.** The working tree is authoritative -- concurrent commits never touch it -- so all three good copies survived. `read-tree HEAD` then re-adding from the worktree restores them; nothing was reconstructed by hand and no other lane`s work was reverted to fix mine.

**The lesson, against the recipe I was given.** `read-tree` once per session is NOT enough: it must immediately precede every commit, because the window between re-seed and commit is exactly where a concurrent writer lands. A pathspec commit does not protect a NEW file either, since an unknown path must be `add`-ed first.

commits.subject: RETRACT my own 2g-1 shortcut: extension-uniformity needs TWO inputs, not one, and this workspace has no Serre duality
commits.summary:
**The retraction.** I posted on the team thread that extension-uniformity reduces to the single scalar $\mathrm{genus}\,C_\kappa = \mathrm{genus}\,C$, via "the threshold can be taken to be $2g-1$". That step IS Serre duality, and there is no Serre duality, canonical divisor or dualizing sheaf anywhere in AJC, AJCR or mathlib (which has none for curves at all). Searched before retracting.

**What the constant really decomposes into,** computed not estimated: $b(\kappa) = \deg_\kappa D_0(\kappa) + \mathrm{genus}\,C_\kappa$, via the new `chi_moduleKSheaf_baseChangeField` ($\chi(\mathcal O_{C_\kappa}) = 1 - \mathrm{genus}\,C_\kappa$). TWO $\kappa$-dependencies: the genus scalar, and the base-divisor degree where the per-field `Classical.choose` survives. The second is not a corollary of the first.

**The reduction, proved.** `uniformVanishing_of_uniform_base_of_genus_invariant` derives the uniform threshold $d+g$ from `UniformBaseDivisor C d` plus genus invariance; monotonicity of the existential bound in $b$ is the whole proof, so $n_0$ never transports. Both `UniformVanishing` and `UniformBaseDivisor` are named `def`s, so the quantifier order is inspectable rather than buried in prose.

**Probe calibrated only on the third attempt.** First Ledger module downstream of a subtree with real sorries (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability`, `Picard/QuotFunctorDef`). Two rounds printed twelve clean lines with a control that failed to RESOLVE; both namespace guesses were wrong, in opposite directions. Now both controls fire `sorryAx` and all 12 declarations read clean, exit 0.

commits.subject: The free half of extension-uniformity is WITNESSED at C_kappa, not asserted of morphism classes
commits.summary:
**One missing instance.** `CurveBaseChange` gave `C_kappa` named `IsProper`/`SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1`/`GeometricallyIntegral` instances but NOT `GeometricallyIrreducible`, which is what the Ledger curve statements bind and which synthesis does not recover from the integral form. Adding it makes every curve-level statement of `FiberBound` fire at `C_kappa` by synthesis alone, proof terms unchanged, with no hypothesis on $\kappa/k$.

**Why the old form read stronger than it was.** r4 stated the free half as `baseChange_binders_stable`, a property of three morphism CLASSES. A class being stable under base change says nothing until an object carries the base-changed instances in the spelling the consumer elaborates against.
